evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Ask which study population and treatment sequence match your plan.
evidence.population: Previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer; FOLFOXIRI compared with FOLFIRI.
evidence.interpretation: In a randomised study of people starting treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer, FOLFOXIRI improved tumour response and time before progression compared with FOLFIRI, and the study found a survival benefit. The more intensive combination also caused more severe side effects, including low white-cell counts, diarrhoea and nerve symptoms. These group results do not predict an individual outcome.

00691.schedule: Phase 1: six FOLFIRINOX cycles, one every 14 days, each with a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. Phase 2: capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–5 of each seven-day week for five weeks, with radiotherapy. Your team supplies the separate radiation calendar.
00691.administration: Phase 1 is six cycles every 14 days: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² and folinic acid 400 mg/m² (200 mg/m² may be considered), irinotecan 180 mg/m², then fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m² continuously over 46 hours; no fluorouracil bolus. Phase 2 is capecitabine 800 mg/m² twice daily on Days 1–5 of each seven-day cycle for five weeks with radiotherapy. NCCP permits a consultant-selected 825 mg/m² alternative; your actual tablet prescription and radiation calendar govern treatment.

evidence.intro: Ask which study population and treatment sequence match your plan.

support.text: Take the prescribed prevention medicines at the planned times and keep rescue treatment available. Tell the team if nausea or constipation is not controlled; do not duplicate steroid or anti-sickness medicines.

support.title: Bowel symptoms
support.text: Report diarrhoea promptly and follow the written rescue plan. Severe symptoms, fever, dehydration or inability to drink need urgent advice.

support.title: Counts and recovery
support.text: White-cell growth-factor injections are prescribed according to individual risk and previous complications. They are not automatically required for every patient or every cycle.

support.title: Cold and nerve symptoms
support.text: Avoid cold exposure as advised after oxaliplatin. Report persistent numbness or difficulty with buttons, walking or everyday tasks before the next dose.

support.title: Blood pressure and wound care
support.text: Keep the agreed blood-pressure and urine checks. Report bleeding, poorly healing wounds, new swelling or severe headache promptly.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Ask which evidence matches your cancer, treatment aim and medicines.
evidence.interpretation: Adding bevacizumab to oxaliplatin chemotherapy delayed cancer progression in the trial reviewed, but did not establish an overall survival improvement. The study pooled two chemotherapy schedules, neither identical to this modified FOLFOX6 regimen. Your team weighs this evidence against side effects and your priorities.

support.text: No routine panitumumab premedication unless previous hypersensitivity/local policy indicates. evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: For selected people whose bowel cancer had already received treatment, adding panitumumab improved tumour shrinkage and delayed progression. A longer overall survival was not established in this analysis.
evidence.interpretation: For selected people whose bowel cancer had already received treatment, adding panitumumab improved tumour shrinkage and delayed progression. A longer overall survival was not established in this analysis.
evidence.population: Prospective-retrospective RAS analysis of second-line metastatic colorectal cancer.
evidence.limitations: The NCCP also includes first-line use, but these figures apply to the second-line analysis.
